extracted.intended_audience: reporters, editors, producers, independent health journalists, and public information officers (PIOs) at academic/government/hospital institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and rules for handling JAMA and JAMA Network embargoed materials, including who may receive prepublication access, what may be done with materials during embargo, distribution and posting rules for PIOs, and enforcement/penalties for embargo violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: The embargo means information concerning the study cannot be published, broadcast, posted online, shared with non-journalists or otherwise placed in the public domain until the time of the embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoed information must not be released to the public in any form before the specified embargo time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepublication access conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network grants prepublication access to articles to selected members of the media who agree not to publish, broadcast, post online, or otherwise place information about embargoed content in the public domain until the time of their publication by the JAMA Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During embargo individuals may read articles, discuss findings with authors, and consult other experts for drafting reports to be released when the article is published. Access is conditional on agreeing to the embargo restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for embargo system
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargo creates a 'level playing field' for journalists and ensures doctors and others have full reports before advising patients; consistency in timing also minimizes potential economic chaos from findings that could influence markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy cites the ICMJE rationale emphasizing fairness to reporters and the need for complete information for clinicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of embargoed materials provided
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the PDF of the full article scheduled for publication, the JAMA Network may provide a news release, video, audio and/or images. All of this material is subject to the embargo and is furnished exclusively for use in coverage of JAMA Network articles and for no other purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All ancillary materials supplied with the article are equally embargoed and must only be used for coverage of the specific JAMA Network article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to additional policies and contact point
rubrics_metrics.description: By requesting access to JAMA Network embargoed materials, members of the media agree to adhere to the above restrictions and also to the following specific policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For additional questions regarding embargo policies contact JAMA Network Media Relations at 312-464-JAMA (5262) or e-mail mediarelations@jamanetwork.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo lift timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes vary and lift the time and day articles are published online or in print (whichever comes first).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should verify the exact embargo time/date/time zone for each article; the lift is tied to the journal's publication timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is eligible for embargoed content credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network will grant credentials to its embargoed content to reporters, writers, editors, and producers from newspapers, magazines, online news services, wire services, radio or television networks and stations; independent journalists and editors who regularly cover health-related topics (Note: Individuals will be required to provide examples of recent work); representatives of academic, government, or hospital media/public relations departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each individual must have their own credentials; credentials are not transferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-transferability of media credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Media credentials are not transferable. Each person accessing the site must have their own credentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing login/access with other individuals or using another person's credentials is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who will not be granted access
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network will not grant access to its embargoed content to public relations firms, advertising agencies, or production companies; writers/editors or other contributors for patient publications created and distributed by industry, such as pharmaceutical companies or device manufacturers; representatives of industry including pharmaceutical companies or device manufacturers; financial or industry analysts; publications or websites supported by industry, including advocacy groups; representatives of corporate media/public relations, advertising, or marketing departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry-affiliated and commercial/marketing entities are excluded from embargoed-access credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo violations: review and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA Network reviews embargo breaks on a case-by-case basis. Circumstances of the embargo violation will be evaluated before a determination is made regarding appropriate penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties may include loss of access to embargoed materials, loss of media credentials to JAMA Network events, and suspension of the media outlet that employs the reporter. Suspended reporters/outlets must reapply after the suspension period ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority over embargo exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The embargo is strict and only JAMA Network Media Relations is authorized to make changes to a study’s embargo time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Media Relations if there is any question regarding an embargo; unofficial or unilateral alterations to embargoes are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: How PIOs learn about new studies
rubrics_metrics.description: I’m a new PIO. How do I hear about new JAMA and JAMA Network studies? You should reach out to JAMA Network Media Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIOs should establish direct contact with Media Relations rather than relying on informal channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting embargoed news releases on websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoed news releases may be posted only to restricted-access websites for journalists. Do not post embargoed news releases to open-access sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricted-access (password-protected or journalist-only) pages are acceptable; public-facing webpages are not until the embargo lifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting or linking to studies
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA and JAMA Network studies cannot be posted on another website, but it is permissible to provide a link to the studies from another website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not repost full articles elsewhere before embargo lifts; providing links is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass distribution to media is prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass distribution of JAMA and JAMA Network papers to the media is not allowed and journalists should be directed to JAMA Network Media Relations and/or the For The Media website for the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations should not send blanket copies of manuscripts to broad media lists; direct media to official channels instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content and distribution restrictions for PIO-prepared releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Any news release or media advisory should have the study’s embargo time, date and time zone at the top of the release or advisory, and cite in which journal the study appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoed news releases should be distributed only to journalists and must not be posted to openly accessible websites or routed to electronic wire services (e.g., PRNewswire, Ascribe, BusinessWire) or otherwise placed in the public domain until the embargo lifts. These open-access services may be used once the embargo lifts.
